Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resource: Observation, unchanged in structure between R4 and R4B. Largely reuses the standard FHIR vital-signs profiles rather than inventing new structure.
Common elements — apply to every vital-sign Observation instance

Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Canonical FHIR ValueSet (required binding): registered | preliminary | final | amended | corrected | cancelled | entered-in-error | unknown. Field vitals are usually 'final' once entered — 'preliminary' is rare in this workflow but keep it available.

Description: Fixed to 'vital-signs' for HR/BP/RR/Temp/SpO2/GCS; 'survey' or a local 'triage' category for the acuity score.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Use the standard category so any FHIR-native vitals viewer/chart in a receiving facility renders these correctly without needing to know your local extensions.

Description: Which vital sign or score this instance represents.
Valueset URL: http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-vitalsignresult (LOINC) for vitals; http://hie.go.ke/fhir/ValueSet/em-triage-acuity-code (local, proposed) for the acuity score
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Reuse canonical LOINC codes rather than inventing local ones for vitals: HR 8867-4, Respiratory Rate 9279-1, Temperature 8310-5, SpO2 59408-5, Blood Pressure panel 85354-9 (components: systolic 8480-6, diastolic 8462-4), GCS total 9269-2 (components: eye-opening, verbal, motor — confirm exact component LOINC codes with your terminology team before finalizing, as these are easy to mis-cite). Vendor systems (Savannah, IntelliSOFT, Konvergenz, Tiberbu, KNH/AfyaApex) are far more likely to already recognize these than a local code.

Description: The encounter this measurement was taken in — typically EMPOCEncounter, or a downstream ED Encounter for repeat measurements.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) — essential for trending vitals across the episode (dispatch snapshot vs on-scene vs in-transit vs ED arrival).

Description: Exact time the measurement was taken.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Non-negotiable for emergency vitals — trending HR/BP/GCS over exact minutes is often the whole clinical point (e.g. deteriorating GCS, worsening shock index).

MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — recommended to always populate in practice, but not forced to 1..1 since some device-sourced vitals (e.g. an automated monitor feed) may not cleanly attribute a human performer.

Description: High/low/critical flag relative to normal range. Maps to vitals.readings[].severity (normal | warning | critical in the real payload).
Comments: UPGRADED TO MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — originally scoped as optional, but real handover data shows this actively drives clinical alerting (e.g. SpO2 80% flagged 'critical'), not just dashboard cosmetics. Map warning/critical from the source system onto the FHIR interpretation codes (e.g. H/HH, L/LL) rather than carrying the source severity string as free text.

Description: Auto-generated clinical guidance text tied to the severity flag, e.g. 'Low oxygen saturation. Start supplemental oxygen and reassess airway and breathing.'
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — newly identified from real handover data. This is clinical decision-support content, not just a label; worth preserving verbatim from the source system rather than discarding once the coded interpretation is captured, since the specific wording may carry protocol-specific instructions.

Description: Qualitative descriptor independent of the numeric value, e.g. pulse 'weak', breathing 'labored'. Maps to readings[].state.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — newly identified from real handover data. This is independent clinical signal (a 'weak' pulse at a normal rate is a different finding from a 'strong' one at the same rate) and must not be silently dropped just because the numeric value already has a slot.

Description: Age-group bucket used to select the applicable reference range for this reading, e.g. adult vs paediatric. Maps to vitals.age_group.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — newly identified from real handover data. Ties directly to EMPatient.extension:isAdult; keep the two consistent for a given patient rather than letting them drift independently across resources.

Description: Normal range for this vital, if your system computes one (e.g. age-adjusted for paediatric HR/RR).

Resource: Value — numeric vitals (HR, RR, Temp, SpO2)

Description: The numeric result with UCUM unit, e.g. HR=110 /min, Temp=38.2 Cel, SpO2=94 %.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) for single-value vitals (HR, RR, Temp, SpO2). Use UCUM units consistently — do not let vendor free-text units leak through (e.g. 'bpm' vs '/min').

Resource: Value — panel vitals with components (Blood Pressure, GCS)

Description: Systolic blood pressure as a component of the BP panel Observation (code=85354-9).
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) when Observation.code = BP panel. MUST SUPPORT.

Description: Diastolic blood pressure as a component of the BP panel Observation.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) when Observation.code = BP panel. MUST SUPPORT.

Description: Individual GCS sub-scores, if your EMT app captures them separately rather than only the total.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..*) — populate when available since sub-scores (especially motor response) carry independent prognostic value beyond the GCS total; not required if your app only captures the total score.

Description: Total Glasgow Coma Score (3–15) when not broken into components.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) when GCS components are not separately captured.

Resource: Triage Score / Acuity — distinct Observation (only if NOT embedded in Encounter.priority)

Description: A standalone, trendable triage acuity record, separate from EMIncidentEncounter.priority (dispatch) and EMPOCEncounter.priority (on-scene) — useful when acuity is reassessed multiple times across the episode and you want each reassessment as its own timestamped record rather than overwriting a single Encounter.priority value.
Comments: OPTIONAL at the profile level — only create this Observation if your workflow needs acuity trending as discrete timestamped events; if a single current-priority value per encounter is sufficient, Encounter.priority alone is enough and this Observation is unnecessary. When used: category, code, value[x], subject, encounter, effectiveDateTime are all REQUIRED on that instance, same as any other Observation on this profile.

Description: The acuity level itself, e.g. an ESI-style 1–5 scale or Low/Medium/High/Critical — reuse the same em-priority-level ValueSet already defined for EMEpisodeOfCare/EMIncidentEncounter/EMPOCEncounter if your scale is identical, rather than defining a second one.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) on the triage-acuity Observation instance, when that instance is used.
